sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains how intellect remains connected to will even after being drawn down, because will stems from the essence of the soul, and similarly a change in reasoning about guilt or merit reflects a change in the will.

translations.translation: And based on this, one can also understand the connection of the intellect
(even after it has been drawn down)
with the will,
for that which through the will the drawing down and revelation of the intellect occurs is because the will is from the essence of the soul,
the essence of all the faculties.
For similarly, it is also regarding the reasoning of "every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil,"
that the change that occurred in this reasoning,
that initially it was a reason for liability and afterwards it became
(this same reasoning itself)
a reason for merit,
is due to the change, so to speak, that occurred in the will
(as explained above in the maamar of the Baal HaHilula).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the cause of a change in will is a new will drawn from the Essence, analogous to a fainting person revived by a strong scent, and above this corresponds to the "sweet savor" of offerings arousing a new will from the Essence beyond revelation.

translations.translation: A)
And now, the reason for this change that occurred in the will
is explained in the maamar,
that after "And the Lord smelled the pleasing aroma,"
the secret of the offering ascends to the secret of Ein Sof,
then a new will is drawn down.
And the concept is as explained by the Admo"r Mahara"sh in the continuation of "Mayim Rabim,"
that a scent arouses the essence of the soul.
For this is like one who faints, heaven forbid,
when they give him a strong scent to smell, he is aroused from his fainting,
for the concept of fainting is the cessation of the diffusion of vitality,
and through the strong scent that arouses the essence of the soul,
vitality is drawn anew
(from the essence of the soul).
And analogously, one can understand Above,
that the concept of "And He was grieved in His heart"
(the opposite of "And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good")
is a movement of withdrawal
(analogous to the concept of fainting),
and through His smelling the pleasing aroma of the offerings,
"It was pleasing before Me that I said and My will was done,"
a new will is drawn from the Essence that is above the aspect of revelation.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that change and regret can apply to a will that has a hidden reason, but not to a will that is above reason, which is the root of the eternity of Israel.

translations.translation: B)
And now, the reason for this, that even in the will
(which is above the intellect)
consolation and regret
(change) can apply,
is because the will is also included in the form of man,
intellect and emotions.
For in the will there are its emotions and its reason,
a hidden reason.
And since intellect
(even a hidden reason)
is something that can be reversed
[as is understood from the reasoning of "every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil," which can be explained in two opposite ways,
for liability and for merit],
therefore,
when a change occurs in the hidden reason,
the will changes
(the emotions within the will),
analogous to the change in revealed intellect through which the emotions change.
For all this is in a will that has a reason.
But a will that is above reason
(which does not have even a hidden reason),
change cannot apply to it.
And this is what is written, "And also the Eternal One of Israel will not relent, for He is not a man that He should relent,"
for the root of the Eternal One of Israel is in the will that is above reason,
and therefore relenting cannot apply to it.
